options.why: Finds $BC$ using Pythagoras' theorem in $\triangle ABC$, but stops there instead of continuing on to find $OM$.
Finds $BM = BC \div 2$ correctly (half of the chord) but gives this half-chord length as $OM$ instead of using Pythagoras' theorem with $OB$ to find the actual perpendicular distance.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ACB = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$BC = \sqrt{AB^2-AC^2} = \sqrt{26^2-10^2} = \sqrt{676-100} = \sqrt{576} = 24$ cm
$OB = 13$ cm (radius, half of $AB$)
$BM = BC \div 2 = 12$ cm (perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord)
$OM = \sqrt{OB^2-BM^2} = \sqrt{13^2-12^2} = \sqrt{169-144} = \sqrt{25} = 5$ cm

$\angle AEB = 76^{\circ} \div 2 = 38^{\circ}$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference)

options.why: Copies the given angle instead of using the angle sum of the right-angled triangle.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ABC = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle)
$\angle BCA = 180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}-28^{\circ} = 62^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)

options.why: Finds $\angle BCD$ but forgets that $CA$ bisects it into two equal parts.
Halves $\angle BAD$ directly instead of first finding $\angle BCD$ from the opposite-angle property.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle BCD = 180^{\circ}-112^{\circ} = 68^{\circ}$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)
$AB = AD$, so $CA$ bisects $\angle BCD$ (equal chords subtend equal angles at the circumference)
$\angle BCA = 68^{\circ} \div 2 = 34^{\circ}$

options.why: Copies $BC$ instead of using Pythagoras' theorem with the shared diameter $BD$.
Adds $AB$ and $BC$ instead of applying Pythagoras' theorem in $\triangle BCD$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle BAD = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle), so $BD = \sqrt{9^2+12^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15$ cm
$\angle BCD = 90^{\circ}$ (angle in a semicircle at $C$)
$DC = \sqrt{BD^2-BC^2} = \sqrt{15^2-12^2} = \sqrt{81} = 9$ cm

options.why: Copies the central angle instead of halving it to find the circumference angle first.
Uses $180^{\circ}$ minus half the central angle instead of the interior angle itself.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ABC = 160^{\circ} \div 2 = 80^{\circ}$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference)
$\angle ADE = \angle ABC = 80^{\circ}$ (exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle)

$AB = CD$, so $\angle AOB = \angle COD$ (equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre)
Both $\angle AEB$ and $\angle CFD$ equal half of their matching central angle, so $\angle CFD = \angle AEB = 27^{\circ}$

options.why: Uses $OM = 8$ correctly but doubles the wrong quantity, or miscalculates $BM$ from $10$ and $8$.
Finds $BM$ correctly but forgets that $M$ is the midpoint of $BD$, so $BD$ is double this.

questions.solution_text:
$O$ lies on $AC$, so $OM \perp BD$ too, and $M$ is the midpoint of $BD$ (perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord).
$OM = 10 - 2 = 8$ cm
$BM = \sqrt{OB^2-OM^2} = \sqrt{10^2-8^2} = \sqrt{36} = 6$ cm
$BD = 2 \times 6 = 12$ cm
